tools.description: Run Sage/Python in the long-lived kernel: stdout, then the repr of the last expression (or '(no output)'). Code runs on the kernel's main thread, one job at a time, so cysignals Sage code works; state persists per session. timeout_s is NOT a computation limit: on expiry you get the partial output and a job id, and the job keeps running (collect it with poll). timeout_s=0 returns at once. A submitted job waits behind the running one ("[queued: another job is running]"); if that one holds the GIL the submit itself is refused after ~10 s ("[kernel busy ...]", the job was not submitted) -- check status or interrupt, then retry.

preparse.description: Apply the Sage preparser (2^10 -> 1024, R.<x> = ...). false runs raw Python (2^10 is XOR).

session.description: Namespace to run in. State persists per session between exec calls.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for the result; 0 = return at once. Never cancels the job.

tools.name: exec

tools.description: Collect a job started by exec. since = the offset the previous call printed (0 to start), so you get only new output. wait_s blocks until the job finishes or that many seconds pass (0 = return immediately, the default).

since.description: Character offset already consumed; the previous call prints the next value.

wait_s.description: Block up to this many seconds waiting for the job to finish (0 = return immediately, the default).

tools.name: poll

tools.description: Empty a session's namespace but keep the session (see drop).

session.description: Namespace to run in. State persists per session between exec calls.

tools.name: reset

tools.description: Free idle sessions; refuses one with a queued/running job (kept, and the job id is reported). all=true drops every idle session.

all.description: Drop every session that has no queued/running job.

tools.name: drop

tools.description: Kernel state (running / busy / not running) with pid and uptime, one line per session with its name count, active jobs, the last error, the log path.
tools.name: status

tools.description: SIGINT the running computation: the job fails with KeyboardInterrupt and the session KEEPS its state -- the first thing to try for a runaway job. Refused when the running job belongs to another MCP client; a no-op when idle: SIGINT can never kill the kernel. force=true is the last resort instead: stop the whole kernel (graceful shutdown, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL), losing every session's variables -- for a computation that ignores SIGINT, e.g. a wedged C-level loop. The next exec starts a fresh kernel and says so; if the signal fails the state files are kept and the pid reported, so a live kernel is never orphaned.

force.description: Stop the kernel itself (all state is lost), not just the job.

tools.name: interrupt

tools.description: Run a file that already exists and return its output inline: exit code, duration, stdout and stderr. Nothing is copied or stored -- the file you name is the file that runs, with cwd = its own directory. lang=auto guesses from the extension and honours a #! for executables; lang=python uses Sage's own interpreter (so `from sage.all import *` works) and lang=sage shells out to `sage`. A non-zero exit or a timeout is an error, with the output attached; the timeout kills the whole process group.

args.description: Arguments appended to the command line.

cwd.description: Working directory (default: the file's own directory).

lang.description: Interpreter; auto uses the extension, then the #! line.

path.description: The file to run (absolute or relative to this server's cwd).

stdin.description: Text fed to the file on stdin.

timeout_s.description: Seconds before the process group is killed.

tools.name: run_file

tools.description: Jupyter notebook helper for the kernels SageMath ships. check: validate and summarise. extract: print the code cells. clear: strip outputs (atomically). run: execute with nbconvert (atomically, to <name>.out.ipynb unless out/in_place is given) and report how many cells ended in error.

out.description: Output path for run/clear (default: <name>.out.ipynb for run, the input file for clear).

timeout_s.description: Overall wall clock budget for run.

tools.name: notebook
